title: Guardrails and permissions
summary: Guardrails check behavior, while permissions limit which operations a system can actually execute.
overview: Input validation and policy checks can reject unsuitable tool requests. Access controls must enforce authority at the execution boundary, rather than relying on a model to obey instructions.
why: A plausible tool call can still target a resource the user is not allowed to change.
example: An incident agent can read service metrics, but a deployment tool checks environment access and requires approval before changing production.
judgment: Decide the permitted resources and actions, and which checks must fail closed.
